newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban gives amnesty to returning exiles.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban gives amnesty to returning exiles.

text.p: The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said on Wednesday a general amnesty has been declared by Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia for all returning refugees, ensuring respect for basic rights.
A statement by the UNHCR's chief of mission for Afghanistan said the declaration was addressed to Afghan refugee communities in Iran, Pakistan and other countries.

"It invites the Afghan refugees to return in safety and dignity to their places of origin, or other areas of their choice, and participate in the reconciliation and reconstruction of the country," it said.

"The amnesty contains all key provisions for ensuring respect for the basic rights of returnees and exempts returnees from exile from prosecution on account of having taken asylum outside, or committing ordinary criminal offences in Afghanistan prior to their departure," the statement said.

"It further exempts returnees from prosecution due to draft evasion, desertion or joining different commanders." The statement said the amnesty also provided "guarantees for the recovery or restitution of property lawfully owned by the returnees and for the respect of their human rights".

"Since the beginning of repatriation of Afghan refugees in mid-1990, this is the first time such a comprehensive amnesty has been issued by the Afghan authorities," the statement quoted UNHCR chief of mission for Afghanistan W. Wijeratne as saying.

More than five million Afghans fled to Pakistan and Iran during the Soviet military occupation of Afghanistan in the 1980s and most of them returned home after Islamic mujahideen guerrillas took over from a collapsed communist government in early 1992.
But many stayed away because of the new round of civil war between rival Afghan factions.

"We anticipate that this (amnesty) declaration will have a positive impact on the pace of repatriation and will give confidence and assurance to the Afghan refugee community to return in safety and dignity," Wijeratne said.
The UNHCR said 20,000 refugees had returned to their homes from Iran and Pakistan in June and it was optimistic that "this trend will accelerate over the summer months".
It said it was launching a "re-energised repatriation programme" in Iran and Pakistan.
The purist Islamic Taleban captured Kabul last September and now control more than two thirds of the country.
